title: Reduce TTFT degradation via weighted router QoS and KV-eviction tuning
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers reported intermittent TTFT spikes and sustained tokens/sec drops across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments when model fan-out and long context windows coincided with regional surges. Investigation indicates the router's fairness heuristics allow bursty tenants to preempt steady low-latency traffic. Combined with aggressive KV-cache eviction under memory pressure, we see increased cold KV lookups and kernel scheduling churn that drive first-token latency up. This ticket implements a short-term mitigation (weighted router QoS + conservative KV-eviction thresholds) and a medium-term follow-up (router admission controls + kernel batch steering).
impact_summary: High: multiple mid-market customers reported production impact during peak hours (up to 6x TTFT for single-token priming, 40-60% drop in sustained tokens/sec on affected hosts). Affected products include chat and streaming endpoints. Root causes span router scheduling, KV-cache churn, and kernel selection thrash under mixed model workloads (rw-13b-v2, rw-70b-quant).
reproduction_steps: Start a regional cluster with mixed workloads: 60% rw-13b-v2 short-chat, 40% rw-70b-quant long-context generation
Drive a burst from 10 synthetic tenants (ramp to 350 RPS) for 2 minutes while maintaining steady 40 RPS background traffic from a high-priority tenant
Observe router queues: weighted fairness imbalance where burst tenants occupy multiplex slots and push low-latency requests to cold-worker assignment
Monitor KV-cache hit rates and observe eviction counts rising followed by increased GPU kernel warmup times and TTFT spikes
Compare tokens/sec on affected worker pods vs baseline under identical hardware
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:12 - Initial customer escalation from AcmeAI reporting 3-5s TTFT spikes on hosted-rw-13b endpoints (Slack #prod-escalations)
03/10 11:00 - Collected pprof traces and router queue dumps; discovered router FIFO policy allows large bursts to monopolize multiplex windows (see dump /tmp/router-dump-0310.tgz)
03/11 02:30 - Observed KV-cache evictions correlate with memory pressure events on dedicated hosts; eviction spikes precede kernel selection oscillation
03/12 16:40 - Ran canary with conservative KV-eviction threshold (-evict-age 30s -> 300s) — saw KV-hit rate improve from 72% -> 93% and TTFT baseline drop ~35% in stress test
03/13 09:50 - Implemented weighted routing prototype giving 2x weight to 'latency' class tenants; preliminary results: reduced first-token tail (95p) by 28% in controlled bench
Telemetry note: affected models show increased kernel-switch events per request (avg 1.9 -> 3.4) during spike windows
mitigation_history: 03/11 - Emergency config: enable conservative kv eviction on regional fleet (config: runtime.kv.evict_threshold=0.65) — reduced immediate evictions but did not fully remove TTFT spikes
03/12 - Rolled a router QoS experiment to 10% of traffic (weighted latency class) — observed partial improvement for high-priority tenants
03/13 - Hotfix PR created to add short-circuit fallback: if router queue depth > 80% then route new low-latency requests to reserved low-latency pool (see PR #5243)
03/13 - Communication sent to affected customers with ETA and temporary mitigation details
decisions: Short-term: ship weighted router QoS + raise KV-eviction age to reduce cold-KV thrash (target rollout to all regions by 2026-03-17)
Medium-term: implement admission control in router (token-bucket per-tenant + reserved slots for latency-class traffic) and a kernel batch steering mechanism to reduce kernel-switch churn
Rollback plan: if tokens/sec drops or P99 TTFT increases post-rollout, revert router QoS change and fall back to existing eviction thresholds while we iterate

acceptance_criteria: 95th-percentile TTFT for latency-class tenants returns to within 1.2x of baseline in mixed-workload synthetic tests
Sustained tokens/sec on representative hosts improves to >80% of pre-surge baseline under test load
KV-cache hit rate stays >=90% during stress tests without causing memory OOMs
No new priority inversion regressions introduced (verified by routing fairness test harness)
Rollout playbook documented and SRE runbook updated
